messages.content:
For breakfast I had a 12 ounce iced coffee and a banana.

For lunch I had a quesadilla

Breakfast four ounces of asparagus, two eggs, one piece of gluten free bread.

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with details about the portion size and the meal it is associated with. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, in specified units. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount. Choose a unit such as 'grams', 'ounces', 'pieces', 'cups', or 'tablespoons'.

meal_name.description: The name of the meal with which the food item is associated. Options include 'breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner', or 'snack'.

Likely they mean breakfast had those items. But they also mention lunch had a quesadilla. So we need to log each food item with portion size, unit, meal name.

We have to call the function log_food for each item. The function signature: food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit (optional), meal_name.

We need to decide portion units: iced coffee 12 ounces, banana? Portion amount unspecified; maybe 1 banana, unit pieces. Quesadilla? Portion amount unspecified; maybe 1 quesadilla, unit pieces. Asparagus 4 ounces, eggs 2 pieces, bread 1 piece.

We need to log each item. The user didn't specify portion units for banana, quesadilla, eggs, bread. We can use default grams? But better to use pieces. The function default is grams if not specified. But we can specify unit. Let's specify for banana: 1 piece. For quesadilla: 1 piece. For eggs: 2 pieces. For bread: 1 piece. For asparagus: 4 ounces. For iced coffee: 12 ounces.
